name: Field Doctor-Style Piri Piri Chicken (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
720 g Chicken
595 g Whole grain rice
1/2 x 400 g tins Plum Tomato
215 g Spinach
1 1/4 Red Peppers
1 1/4 Green Peppers
1 1/2 medium Carrots
110 g Fennel
9 tbsp Mixed Herbs
3/4 tbsp Tomato Puree [tomato]
1/8 Lemon Juice
1 3/4 tsp Sweet Noble Paprika
1 1/2 tsp Parsley Flat
1/4 tsp Red Wine Vinegar
1/4 tsp Tapioca Starch
1/3 tsp Smoked Paprika
1/3 tsp Lemon Zest
1/8 tsp Brown Sugar
0.8 g Sundried Tomatoes [Sundried tomatoes, Salt]
1/8 tsp Chicken Stock (Chicken Extract, Chicken Fat, Salt], Sea Salt, Red Chilli, Chipotle chilli
directions:
1. Rice: Cook wholegrain rice until tender; drain and keep warm.

2. Piri sauce: Soften red pepper, green pepper, carrot and fennel in extra virgin olive oil. Add chopped tomato, tomato puree, sundried tomatoes, lemon juice, lemon zest, red wine vinegar, sweet and smoked paprika, chilli/chipotle to taste, brown sugar, herb mix and chicken stock. Simmer until thick; blend partly or leave chunky. Thicken with tapioca slurry if needed.

3. Chicken: Season chicken and brown in a little oil, then simmer in the piri sauce until cooked through.

4. Finish: Wilt spinach into the sauce. Serve over rice with parsley.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.
description:
Ingredients: Chicken, Whole grain rice, Water, Chopped Tomato, Spinach, Red Pepper, Green Pepper, Carrot...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Piri Piri Chicken (Low FODMAP) (~365 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/peri-peri-chicken
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~365 g x 8 = 2920 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~216 g (inferred ~7.41% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~47 g (inferred ~1.61% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
